tools.name: duckdb_data_query
tools.desc: Query data with DuckDB SQL and get the rows back as JSON (or CSV, or a Markdown table): files and globs (CSV, JSON, Parquet, Excel), URLs, S3 and Azure paths, the previous flow step's output (the table input), and databases attached read-only (Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, Oracle, DuckDB files). Reads, joins, filters, transforms and aggregates in one query; save_to also writes the result to a CSV, JSON or Parquet file.

params.name: sql
params.desc: The DuckDB SQL. Several statements run in turn; the last one's rows are the result. Tables: the sources' names, input, and connection.schema.table
params.example: SELECT region, sum(total) AS revenue FROM orders GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC

params.name: sources
params.desc: Tables to query: {"name": "location"}. A location is a file, glob, URL, s3:// path, or a folder ending in / (every Parquet, CSV and JSON file under it, sub-folders too, read as one table with a filename column; year=2026/ folders become columns). Or {"path": ..., "format": "parquet|csv|json", "filename": false, "hive": false}

params.name: connections
params.desc: Databases to attach, as many as needed and of any types (read-only unless "read_only": false): [{"name", "type": postgres | mysql | sqlite | sqlserver | oracle | duckdb, "dsn": "…"}] or the parts {"name", "type", "host", "port", "database" (Oracle: "service" or "sid"), "user", "password"}. dsn can be key=value, a URL or a JDBC string (jdbc:postgresql://…, jdbc:oracle:thin:@//host:1521/SERVICE); user and password are added to it. Give each database its own password as ${DB_<NAME>} (e.g. "password": "${DB_SALES}"): SpecWright asks for it once and keeps it as a secret. "schema" limits a Postgres connection to one schema. In SQL: name.schema.table, or postgres_query('name', '…') to run SQL on the database itself. Kerberos: "auth": "kerberos" logs in with your Kerberos ticket instead of a password (or "keytab" and "principal" for a ticket of its own; "krb5_conf"; "kerberos_service"). Oracle: logs in as /@target with a sqlnet.ora written for the run (the ticket must be in a file: "ticket_cache": "FILE:…", KRB5CCNAME, or a keytab). Postgres: DuckDB's driver has no Kerberos, so the tables listed in "tables" (["public.orders"] or {"recent": "SELECT …"}) are read with psql and queried as name.schema.table.

params.name: extensions
params.desc: DuckDB extensions to load as well, comma-separated (those the sources and connections need load by themselves); community ones as name@community

params.name: input
params.desc: A file with the previous step's output (in a flow: {{input_file}}), queried as the table input

params.name: save_to
params.desc: Also write the whole result to this file: .csv, .json, .jsonl or .parquet, local or s3://

params.name: max_rows
params.desc: At most this many rows in the answer (save_to writes all of them)

params.name: save_mode
params.desc: overwrite save_to, or append the rows to what it already holds (accumulate results across runs; columns matched by name)

secrets.name: DB_*
secrets.desc: Database passwords, one per connection: write ${DB_SALES} (any name starting DB_) in a connection's password or dsn and SpecWright asks for it once

secrets.name: PGPASSWORD
secrets.desc: Postgres password read by the driver when a connection gives none (for several databases, use DB_* names instead)

secrets.name: MYSQL_PWD
secrets.desc: MySQL password (read by the MySQL driver)

secrets.name: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
secrets.desc: AWS access key for S3 (otherwise your AWS profile or SSO is used)

secrets.name: AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
secrets.desc: AWS session token for S3 (temporary credentials)

secrets.name: ORACLE_PASSWORD
secrets.desc: Oracle password, used as ${ORACLE_PASSWORD} in a dsn (for several Oracle databases, use DB_* names instead)

secrets.name: MSSQL_PASSWORD
secrets.desc: SQL Server password, used as ${MSSQL_PASSWORD} in a dsn

secrets.name: AWS_REGION
secrets.desc: AWS region of the S3 buckets (e.g. eu-west-1)

secrets.name: AWS_ENDPOINT_URL
secrets.desc: Endpoint of S3-compatible storage (MinIO, Cloudflare R2, Ceph), e.g. http://minio.internal:9000

guide.summary: Queries data with DuckDB SQL: the previous step's output, files and whole folders (CSV, JSON, Parquet, Excel), URLs, S3 (and S3-compatible storage) and Azure, and databases (Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, Oracle). One query reads, joins, filters and aggregates; results come back as JSON, CSV or a Markdown table, and can be saved or accumulated in a file.
when: A previous step gives JSON or CSV rows you want to filter, group or sum without an AI step.
You need to join a file with a database table, or two databases with each other.
A folder of files (a data lake prefix on S3, daily exports) should be read as one table.
A report needs totals or a Markdown table from data in files or cloud storage.
You want a result saved as CSV, JSON or Parquet for another system.
A scheduled flow should build up a history: each run appends its rows to one file.
how: Pass the previous step's output with input = {{input_file}}; it is the table input (JSON or CSV is detected).

Name files, globs, URLs, s3:// paths or folders (ending in /) in sources ({"events": "s3://bucket/events/"}) and query them by that name. A folder reads every data file under it as one table, with a filename column and year=2026/ folders as columns.

Attach databases in connections, as many as you need and of any types, each with its own name and connect string; give each its own password as ${DB_<NAME>} ("password": "${DB_SALES}") and SpecWright asks for it once (save it to the keychain for scheduled runs). JDBC strings work too. In SQL, use name.schema.table, or postgres_query('name', '…') to run SQL on the database itself.

Kerberos (no password): add "auth": "kerberos" to a postgres or oracle connection. It uses the ticket from kinit, or "keytab" and "principal" for unattended runs. Oracle logs in as /@service (its client needs the ticket in a file); Postgres tables listed in "tables" are read with psql (libpq with GSSAPI) and queried as name.schema.table.
S3: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY when set (as secrets), otherwise your AWS profile or SSO; AWS_REGION; AWS_ENDPOINT_URL for MinIO, R2 or Ceph.
Choose format json for later steps (fields like {{run.buffer_output.json[0].revenue}}), markdown for reports, csv for files.
Several statements run in turn; the last one's rows are the result. save_to writes every row (save_mode append adds them to what the file holds); max_rows limits only the answer.

examples.title: Group the previous step's JSON
examples.text: Open orders by region from a JSON array the step before gives (here, sample orders).

args.sql:
SELECT region, count(*) AS orders, sum(total) AS revenue
FROM input
WHERE status = 'open'
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY revenue DESC

examples.title: CSV to a Markdown table
examples.text: Sorts CSV rows and returns them as a Markdown table for a report.

args.sql: SELECT * FROM input ORDER BY price DESC

examples.result:
| sku | name | price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HD-12 | Headset | 89 |
| KB-01 | Keyboard | 49 |
| MS-07 | Mouse | 19 |

examples.title: Plain SQL, no data needed
examples.text: Generates rows with SQL alone: the next three days.

args.sql:
SELECT range AS day, strftime(DATE '2026-11-01' + range::INT, '%Y-%m-%d') AS date
FROM range(3)

examples.title: Several statements, saved as Parquet
examples.text: Builds a table, then counts by status; every row is also written to a Parquet file.

args.sql:
CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT * FROM input;
SELECT status, count(*) AS n FROM t GROUP BY status ORDER BY status

examples.title: Accumulate results in a file
examples.text: Appends this run's totals to a CSV file (save_mode append): run it again and the file holds both runs. Use an s3:// path to keep the history in S3.

args.sql:
SELECT region, sum(total) AS revenue, current_date AS day
FROM input
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY region

examples.title: A whole S3 folder as one table
examples.text: Every Parquet, CSV and JSON file under the prefix (sub-folders too) as one table; filename tells which file a row came from, and region=eu/ folders become a column. Needs your bucket and AWS credentials.

args.sql:
SELECT region, count(*) AS events, count(DISTINCT filename) AS files
FROM events
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY events DESC

examples.title: Two Postgres databases and Oracle in one query
examples.text: Each database has its own connect string and its own password (DB_SALES, DB_CRM, DB_HR: asked for once, then kept as secrets). The query joins across all three. Needs your servers.

args.sql:
SELECT o.region, sum(o.total) AS revenue, r.manager, h.headcount
FROM sales.public.orders o
JOIN crm.crm.regions r USING (region)
JOIN hr.HR.REGION_HEADCOUNT h ON h.REGION = o.region
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY revenue DESC

examples.title: Kerberos: Oracle and Postgres without passwords
examples.text: Both connections log in with a Kerberos ticket from a service keytab (no passwords anywhere). The Oracle side is attached live; the Postgres tables are read with psql. Needs your KDC, servers, Oracle Instant Client and psql.

args.sql:
SELECT h.REGION AS region, h.HEADCOUNT AS headcount, sum(o.total) AS revenue
FROM hr.HR.REGION_HEADCOUNT h
JOIN sales.public.orders o ON o.region = h.REGION
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY revenue DESC

examples.title: Ask Postgres itself
examples.text: Runs SQL on an attached Postgres database (needs a reachable server and the PGPASSWORD secret). Plain SELECT version() would be DuckDB's version.
